factErrors: At predict-meet/altitude-c/done, the universal claim that the three altitudes are concurrent is concluded from four fixed coordinate examples; these figures verify only those cases, and no general proof or explicit “illustration only” qualification is supplied.

In the altitude-a misconception, the correction says that in an obtuse triangle the foot lies on an extension of BC without the necessary condition. Exactly two altitude feet are outside; the foot from the obtuse vertex is on the opposite segment. In the supplied obtuse preset, Ha=(6/17,24/17) is on segment BC.

issues.problem: The initial definition says an altitude is dropped to the opposite side, although in an obtuse triangle its foot may lie on an extension of that side.
issues.fix: Define an altitude from the outset as the line through a vertex perpendicular to the line containing the opposite side.

issues.problem: The foot and orthocenter coordinates are announced without any calculation, so students are not shown how the values or the concurrence in each example are obtained.
issues.fix: Work at least one exact example using projection, slopes, or vector equations, then explain that the other displayed coordinates are rounded calculations.

issues.problem: The dot product is introduced without definition and may exceed the prerequisite level of the lesson.
issues.fix: Define the vectors and the zero-dot-product criterion, or replace this hint with a compass-and-straightedge or coordinate-slope method.

issues.problem: The same yes/no prediction is asked twice in immediate succession, weakening the pause for student reasoning.
issues.fix: Ask once after frame 2, wait for a response, then reveal H in frame 3 without repeating the question.

issues.problem: A, H, Hb, and Hc all have coordinates (0,0), so their labels, segments, and highlights can overlap and obscure the important right-triangle edge case.
issues.fix: Use leader lines or offset labels for the coincident points and distinguish the corresponding altitude lines by color or line style.

issues.problem: It invites students to drag a vertex, but the walkthrough provides only fixed preset frames and no specified dragging control.
issues.fix: Add an actual dynamic vertex control, or change the invitation to an exercise using paper or separate geometry software.
